registration.title: Registration numbers for furnished rentals & platforms in 2026
registration.intro: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 requires platforms to verify a valid registration number for every short-term rental listing. In France, hosts must reconcile existing municipal rules with the upcoming national API Meublés portal.

eu.title: EU framework (Regulation 2024/1028)
eu.body: In force since 20 May 2026, the regulation harmonizes short-term rental registration across the EU. Platforms like Airbnb and Booking must collect and verify the registration number (NER) before publishing or maintaining a listing.

france.title: France: furnished tourism declaration
france.body: Depending on your municipality, you may need to declare or register your furnished rental (13-digit number in tense zones, town hall procedures elsewhere). The national API Meublés portal is expected in Q4 2026. Keep your municipal numbers in the meantime.

platforms.title: Platform checks from September 2026
platforms.body: Major platforms are tightening NER checks from September 2026. Without a valid number or proof of regularization, your listing may be blocked. Prepare your documents and track status per channel.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not file on your behalf with town halls or official portals, it centralizes number tracking, city playbooks, platform blocks and appeal evidence, with a clear next action per property.

frNerMigration.title: France NER national migration 2026: furnished rental guide
frNerMigration.intro: France is moving furnished tourist rentals to a national teleservice (API Meublés / Démarche Numérique), expected in Q4 2026. Existing municipal numbers will need renewal within a transition window; after that, old numbers may become invalid. Platforms will require a valid national NER.

timeline.title: Timeline (configurable in Glint)
timeline.body: National portal expected Q4 2026. Transition end date will be published by the State at launch. Host Registry stores dates in playbook config, not hardcoded in every screen.

inventory.title: Inventory your local numbers
inventory.body: For each French property, record your current municipal registration number and issuing commune. If you are not yet registered locally, you will likely need to register everywhere when the national portal opens.

dossier.title: Prepare your dossier
dossier.body: Gather ID, address proof, municipal registration proof, listing URLs and co-ownership or change-of-use documents if applicable. Use the NER Migration Cockpit checklist in Glint.

platforms.title: Update listings after NER
platforms.body: When you receive your NER, update Airbnb, Booking, Vrbo and other channels. Mark each channel in the migration wizard. Listing Health URLs are informational; channel update completion is tracked on the migration record.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not submit to Démarche Numérique or mairies. It inventories numbers, tracks checklist progress, stores a notify-on-open preference (storage only in v1), and guides you through recording the NER and updating channels.

ses.title: SES Hospedajes, Mossos & Ertzaintza: Spain guest reporting
ses.intro: In Spain, tourist rental hosts must transmit guest data within 24 hours of arrival. The applicable system depends on the region: SES.HOSPEDAJES for most of the country, Mossos in Catalonia and Ertzaintza in the Basque Country.

ses.title: SES.HOSPEDAJES (Ministerio del Interior)
ses.body: The Sistema de Hospedajes (SES) covers most autonomous communities. Annex I data must be submitted via the Ministry of Interior MIR portal within 24h. Glint validates fields and runs SOAP dry-runs by default. Live MIR submission is optional and requires explicit per-property activation.

mossos.title: Mossos d'Esquadra (Catalonia)
mossos.body: In Catalonia, SES does not apply: reporting goes through the Mossos Hotels portal. SES-only tools leave Catalan hosts without integrated coverage, Glint collects Annex I data and exports in the expected format for manual submission.

ertzaintza.title: Ertzaintza (Basque Country)
ertzaintza.body: In the Basque Country (Ertzaintza territory), reporting is handled by Ertzaintza. As in Catalonia, there is no standard public API, Glint prepares data and tracks 24h deadlines.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Annex I check-in register, due queue with 48h prep window, field validation and fitxa/CSV export. You submit on your region's official portal. Glint does not replace your MIR declarant identity.

guestRegister.title: Guest police fiche: obligations for hosts in France
guestRegister.intro: When renting a furnished property to a foreign-national guest, the host must have them complete and sign an individual police form on arrival. This obligation is separate from the furnished tourism registration number.

obligation.title: Who is affected?
obligation.body: Any host renting to a non-French guest (with some EU exceptions) must collect a police fiche. French guests may be registered optionally depending on your internal workflow.

data.title: What information to collect?
data.body: Identity, nationality, date and place of birth, address, stay dates, signature. Glint provides a public link or QR with compliant fields and digital signature.

retention.title: Retention and transmission
retention.body: Forms must be kept for 6 months after departure. They are only transmitted to law enforcement on official request. Glint does not send them automatically.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Shareable check-in link, missing-fiche alerts, CSV export and PDF printing, integrated into each property's guest register with configured retention.

amsterdamNightCap.title: Amsterdam & Netherlands: night caps, permit & registration
amsterdamNightCap.intro: In the Netherlands, tourist rental from your primary residence combines mandatory national registration, a municipal holiday permit (notably in Amsterdam), notification before each stay, and night caps. These obligations are separate from France's furnished tourism registration number or Italy's CIN.

registration.title: National registration (registratietoeristischeverhuur.nl)
registration.body: Since 2024, every short-term rental must be registered on the national portal registratietoeristischeverhuur.nl. The number is free and must appear on all listings. Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 (applicable from 20 May 2026), platforms verify this number before publishing or maintaining a listing.

permit.title: Holiday-rental permit (Amsterdam vergunning)
permit.body: In Amsterdam, the national number alone is not enough: a separate home-sharing vergunning is required for primary residences (approximately €76 in 2026, with renewal). Without a valid permit, you risk fines. Other gemeenten (Rotterdam, The Hague, Utrecht) apply similar rules. Verify locally on amsterdam.nl and municipal portals.

nightCap.title: Night caps: 30 / 15 nights
nightCap.body: For primary residences in Amsterdam: 30 rental nights per calendar year citywide. From 1 April 2026, eight wijken are capped at 15 nights/year: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde, De Weteringschans, Grachtengordel-West, Grachtengordel-Zuid, Haarlemmerbuurt, Jordaan, Nieuwmarkt/Lastage and Oude Pijp. Other Dutch municipalities also enforce night caps. Check rijksoverheid.nl.

notification.title: Municipal notification before each stay
notification.body: Before every guest stay, you must notify Amsterdam via the official portal (amsterdam.nl, notify stay). Prepare registration number, permit number, dates and guest count. Glint tracks upcoming stays and prepares copy fields. You submit manually on the municipal portal.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not file on your behalf with registratietoeristischeverhuur.nl or gemeente portals, it centralizes national number tracking, permit status, per-stay notifications and night counting (30/15), with a clear next action per property.

italyCinAlloggiati.title: Italy: CIN (BDSR) and Alloggiati Web for hosts
italyCinAlloggiati.intro: In Italy, two distinct national obligations apply to short-term rental hosts: the Codice Identificativo Nazionale (CIN) for platform listings, and the Alloggiati Web schedina for border police. Neither replaces regional CIR/SCIA or France's guest police fiche.

cin.title: CIN via BDSR portal (Ministry of Tourism)
cin.body: From 20 May 2026, platforms verify your CIN under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 and may depublish non-compliant listings. Register on il turismo con il codice (BDSR) with SPID or CIE. The CIN must appear on Airbnb, Booking.com and all OTAs. Fines up to €8,000 for missing CIN on listings.

alloggiati.title: Alloggiati Web: schedina within 24h
alloggiati.body: Under TULPS art. 109, communicate each guest's schedina to Polizia di Stato within 24 hours of check-in via alloggiatipoliziadistato.it. Complete the establishment alta on the portal first, then file each schedina with identity, nationality, date and place of birth, document type and arrival date.

distinct.title: Three separate obligations
distinct.body: CIN (tourism / platforms) ≠ Alloggiati schedina (police) ≠ regional CIR/SCIA (planning). Do not confuse the code displayed on Airbnb with police reporting. Many regions also require monthly ISTAT tourist flow statistics (ROSS 1000, Sinfonia). Submit on your regional portal, with no Glint API integration.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not submit to BDSR or Alloggiati Web, it tracks CIN per listing, collects schedina fields via check-in link, validates data and prepares CSV/printable export with a 24h due queue. You submit on official portals.

portugalRnalSiba.title: Portugal: RNAL and SIBA for Alojamento Local hosts
portugalRnalSiba.intro: In Portugal, Alojamento Local registration (RNAL) covers your platform listings, while SIBA covers police reporting for foreign guests. Portuguese nationals are not reported to SIBA. These obligations are separate from Spain's SES declarations or France's guest police fiche.

rnal.title: RNAL: Registo Nacional de Alojamento Local
rnal.body: Register your short-term rental with Turismo de Portugal and your municipality (comunicação prévia). You receive an RNAL number (e.g. 12345/AL) to display on all listings. From 20 May 2026, platforms verify RNAL under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028.

siba.title: SIBA: Boletim de Alojamento (foreign guests)
siba.body: Hosts lodging foreign guests for pay must register the establishment on siba.ssi.gov.pt (SSI/UCFE) and submit a Boletim de Alojamento for each foreign guest arrival AND departure. Portuguese nationals are not reported. Fines €100–€2,000 for late communication (Lei 23/2007 art. 203).

phases.title: SIBA reporting phases
phases.body: Phase 1: register the establishment on the SIBA portal. Phase 2: for each stay: report foreign guest arrival within 3 working days (dias úteis). Phase 3: report departure within 3 working days after checkout. Glint prepares boletim fields via check-in link and CSV/printable export. You enter manually on the official portal.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not submit to Turismo de Portugal or SIBA, it tracks RNAL per listing, collects boletim data, validates fields and manages the due queue (3 working days) for arrival and departure. You remain legally responsible for submission.

greeceAmaAade.title: Greece: AMA (AADE) and stay declarations
greeceAmaAade.intro: In Greece, the AMA (Αριθμός Μητρώου Ακινήτου) is your listing registration number, while the Short-Term Stay Declaration (Δήλωση Βραχυχρόνιας Διαμονής) is a separate per-stay obligation on myAADE. Glint prepares exports, with no automatic filing and no live government API.

ama.title: AMA: AADE property registry registration
ama.body: Register each short-term rental unit in the AADE Short-Term Stay Property Registry via myAADE (aade.gr). You receive an AMA to display on Airbnb, Booking.com and other OTAs. Licensed tourist accommodations may use an ESL or Unique Notification Number instead. From 20 May 2026, platforms verify numbers under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028. Missing AMA on listings is commonly cited at €5,000.

declaration.title: AADE stay declaration (≤59 nights)
declaration.body: For each short-term stay (≤59 nights), submit the declaration on myAADE by the 20th of the calendar month following guest departure (e.g. checkout 15 July → declare by 20 August). Stays of 60+ nights use the long-term lease declaration path, outside Glint's short-stay queue. Collect identity, nationality, arrival and departure dates.

distinct.title: AMA ≠ stay declaration
distinct.body: AMA covers listing compliance; the stay declaration covers each guest after checkout. From October 2025, Greece also applies updated property safety and operational requirements (fire safety, equipment), see the AADE short-term rental hub. Several municipalities (Athens, Thessaloniki) restrict new AMA registrations in certain zones from 2026.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not submit to AADE, it tracks AMA per listing, collects guest data via check-in link, validates fields and prepares CSV/printable export with a due queue (by the 20th of the month after departure). You submit manually on myAADE.

belgiumStrRegistration.title: Belgium short-term rental registration (2026)
belgiumStrRegistration.intro: Belgium has no single national STR registration number. Hosts must comply with Brussels-Capital, Flanders or Wallonia rules before listing on Airbnb or Booking. Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 requires platforms to verify registration numbers from 20 May 2026.

regions.title: Three regions, three systems
regions.body: Brussels-Capital: prior declaration dossier to Brussels Economy and Employment before any rental (1–90 consecutive nights). Flanders: mandatory aanmelding at Toerisme Vlaanderen under the Logiesdecreet, even occasional Airbnb. Wallonia: compulsory registration with Tourisme Wallonie before guests arrive, including fire safety and planning compliance.

eu.title: EU 2024/1028 and platform checks
eu.body: Platforms verify registration numbers and may report activity via SDEP where Member States require it. Display your regional number on every OTA listing once issued.

glint.title: How Glint helps (honest product)
glint.body: Glint does not submit government forms and has no fake Belgium API. We route your property to the correct regional playbook, track dossier checklist items (fire safety, insurance, urban planning), registration status and listing display, with official deep links and next-action priority.

brusselsAirbnbRegistration.title: Brussels Airbnb registration: prior declaration
brusselsAirbnbRegistration.intro: In Brussels-Capital, you must file a prior declaration dossier before renting your property for tourist accommodation, including occasional stays and principal residence, for stays of 1 to 90 consecutive nights.

dossier.title: Prior declaration dossier
dossier.body: Gather ID, criminal record extract, insurance proof, fire safety certificate (ASI/ACS), urban planning compliance, floor plans and entrance photos. Private and professional operators use different forms on economy-employment.brussels. The registration number is issued only after a complete conforming file.

logo.title: Logo and platform display
logo.body: Once approved, display the official logo near the property entrance and add your registration number to Airbnb, Booking.com and all OTAs. Platforms verify numbers under EU 2024/1028.

tax.title: Brussels tourist tax
tax.body: Register with Brussels Fiscality for tourist tax on overnight stays. Glint links to official guidance, no automatic commune tax engine.

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Track dossier progress, operator category, submission date and registration number in one place. Glint prepares your checklist and export. You file on the official Brussels portal.

croatiaEvisitor.title: Croatia: accommodation categorisation and eVisitor
croatiaEvisitor.intro: In Croatia, you must obtain official tourist accommodation categorisation before advertising, then register every guest on eVisitor within 24 hours of arrival and report departure within 24 hours of checkout. Sojourn tax (boravišna pristojba) is calculated from eVisitor data.

categorisation.title: Tourist accommodation categorisation / approval
categorisation.body: Before any listing, obtain approval and categorisation from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport (mint.gov.hr). Your property must be registered as a tourist accommodation facility. Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1028, platforms verify registration from 20 May 2026; Croatia's unique listing registration numbers are expected from ~January 2027 under the new Hospitality Act / eTourism.

evisitor.title: eVisitor: property object registration
evisitor.body: Create an account at evisitor.hr and register your accommodation object. You need the object ID for guest check-in and check-out reporting. Categorisation and eVisitor are separate obligations: one covers the listing, the other mandatory guest reporting since 2016.

reporting.title: Arrival / departure reporting within 24h
reporting.body: Register every guest on eVisitor within 24 hours of arrival (check-in) and report departure within 24 hours of checkout. Tourism inspectors check pre-season and peak season. Glint collects fields via check-in link, validates data and prepares CSV/printable export. You submit manually on evisitor.hr. No live API in this release (Rhetos integration planned for phase 2).

glint.title: How Glint helps
glint.body: Glint does not submit to eVisitor, it tracks categorisation and object ID, collects guest data, validates fields and manages the 24h due queue for arrival and departure. You remain legally responsible for submission on the official portal.

1.a: Glint is an EU short-term rental compliance cockpit for hosts and small property managers. It combines guided city playbooks, a next-action engine, guest register and reporting queues, registration tracking, iCal stay sync, and portfolio tools. Glint prepares your steps and exports. You submit on official portals.

2.a: Independent hosts and small managers with one or many listings on Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, and similar platforms. It fits portfolios across France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Greece, Croatia, the Netherlands, and Belgium, especially when you need one bilingual FR/EN workspace instead of several single-country tools.

3.q: Does Glint file compliance steps with authorities for me?
3.a: No. Glint does not replace local authorities. It guides you through compliance tunnels, links official forms and rules, and helps you track numbers, guest register, listings, and deadlines. You remain the filing identity on government portals. Glint is software only: not a certification body, not a law firm, not a notified body.

4.a: In force since 20 May 2026, this regulation requires hosts to obtain a registration number and platforms to verify it before publishing EU listings. In France, keep your municipal number until the national API Meublés portal opens (expected Q4 2026). Glint tracks both regimes and helps you prepare for the transition.

5.q: Which countries and cities have guided playbooks?
5.a: Full city tunnels ship for France (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice, plus other French cities via adaptable templates), Spain (Madrid, Valencia, Málaga, Barcelona, Bilbao, Donostia-San Sebastián, Vitoria-Gasteiz), Italy (Roma, Milano, Firenze, Venezia), Portugal (Lisboa, Porto, Faro, Funchal), Greece (Athina, Thessaloniki, Heraklion, Rhodes, Corfu), Croatia (Zagreb, Split, Dubrovnik, Zadar), the Netherlands (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Den Haag, Utrecht), and Belgium (Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent, Bruges, Liège, Namur), each with a country-level fallback guide.

6.q: How do guided playbooks and the next-action engine work?
6.a: Each property gets a step-by-step playbook keyed to country and city, with official portal links and residency branching where it applies. The next-action engine surfaces the priority step per property so you know what to do now, without spreadsheets or scattered folders.

7.a: A public check-in link or QR that collects the right guest fields for your jurisdiction: French fiche de police for foreign guests, Spain Annex I (SES, Mossos, or Ertzaintza), Italy Alloggiati schedina, Portugal SIBA boletim, Greece AADE stay data, and Croatia eVisitor fields. Hosts get signature capture where required, retention windows that match local rules, CSV or print export, and due queues with deadlines.

8.q: Does Glint sync stays from iCal?
8.a: Yes. Paste Airbnb, Booking, Vrbo, Google Calendar, or other HTTPS iCal feeds per property. Glint syncs upcoming stays into your stay registry for missing-fiche tracking, night-cap counting, and reporting queues. Feeds typically expose dates and a guest label only, so guests still complete the full form via the check-in link.

9.q: Does Glint submit SES.HOSPEDAJES reports live by default?
9.a: No. Glint validates guest data and runs dry-run checks by default. Live MIR submission is optional and requires an explicit live mode plus per-property enablement. We never replace your MIR filing identity.

10.q: What about Catalonia and the Basque Country?
10.a: SES.HOSPEDAJES does not apply there. Mossos Hotels covers Catalonia and Ertzaintza covers the Basque Country. SES-only tools leave those hosts behind. Glint collects Annex I data, validates it, exports a fitxa or CSV, and tracks the due queue. You submit on the official portal.

11.q: Does Glint cover Italy (CIN and Alloggiati)?
11.a: Yes. Glint tracks BDSR CIN for listing compliance under EU 2024/1028 and prepares Alloggiati Web guest schedules (within 24h after check-in) with export kits and due queues. CIN and Alloggiati are separate obligations. We do not submit to government systems automatically.

12.q: Does Glint cover Portugal, Greece, and Croatia?
12.a: Yes. Portugal: RNAL for listings plus SIBA boletim for foreign guests within 3 working days. Greece: AMA for listings plus AADE Short-Term Stay Declarations (by the 20th of the month after departure). Croatia: tourist categorisation tracking plus eVisitor check-in and check-out within 24h. In each case Glint prepares export kits and queues. You submit on the official portal.

13.q: Does Glint cover the Netherlands and Belgium?
13.a: Yes. Netherlands: national registration number, holiday-rental permit tracking, Amsterdam per-stay municipal notification queue, and the 30/15 night-cap engine for Amsterdam wijken. Belgium: tri-regional registration for Brussels prior declaration, Flanders aanmelding, and Wallonia registration, with region routing, dossier checklist, and listing display tracking. No fake government API push.

14.q: Does Glint track the 120-night primary residence cap?
14.a: Yes, for French properties marked as primary residence. Glint counts nights from iCal feeds and manual stays, applies the statutory cap (120) or commune cap (90 in Paris, Lyon, Nice), and alerts you before you breach, under Code du tourisme art. L324-1-1.

15.q: If Airbnb collects taxe de séjour, am I done?
15.a: No. When platforms act as tiers collecteur you must still declare each period on your commune or EPCI portal, often monthly, including €0 months and stays collected via the platform. Glint tracks taxable nights and queues declaration periods. You submit on the official portal. There is no automated filing.

16.q: What are the plans and prices?
16.a: Starter is €19/month for up to 3 active properties. Pro is €49/month for up to 50 active properties. Every plan includes a 14-day free trial and you can cancel anytime. Both include guided playbooks, guest register, expiry alerts, FR + EN interface, Listing Health score, the France NER migration cockpit (where applicable), and Compliance Evidence Pack PDF export. Pro adds bulk export, archiving, and priority support.

17.q: Can I archive a property without losing data?
17.a: Yes. Archiving removes the property from your active portfolio and plan limit while keeping compliance steps, guest register, and history. Restore in one click.

18.a: Guest and compliance records stay in your account for the retention windows required by each jurisdiction (for example 6 months for the French fiche). Glint builds operational registries for European compliance and is software only: not a certification body, not a law firm, not a notified body. You remain responsible for filings. Full details are in the Privacy Policy and Terms linked in the footer.

19.a: Use in-app help from your dashboard, and Pro plans include priority support. Legal pages and country guides in the footer cover registration numbers, SES regions, guest register, Amsterdam night caps, Italy CIN and Alloggiati, Portugal RNAL and SIBA, Greece AMA and AADE, Croatia eVisitor, and Belgium registration.

panel.title: AADE Short-Term Stay Declaration
panel.description: {city} — Greece requires a Short-Term Stay Declaration (Δήλωση Βραχυχρόνιας Διαμονής) per stay (≤59 nights) by the 20th of the month after guest departure. Glint prepares declaration data; you submit on myAADE.
panel.honestyNote: Glint does not submit to AADE automatically. We collect → validate → export CSV/printable kit → you submit on https://www.aade.gr/myAADE. You remain legally responsible.
panel.step1: Register property in AADE registry and obtain AMA (or ESL for licensed tourist accommodation)
panel.step2: Enable check-in link and collect guest data for AADE declaration fields
panel.step3: Prepare export kit (printable + CSV) after guest departure
panel.step4: Submit Short-Term Stay Declaration on myAADE by day 20 of the month after checkout
panel.step5: Mark submission status in Glint (prepared → submitted → accepted)
panel.longTermNote: Stays of 60+ nights use the AADE long-term lease declaration path — not included in the short-term due queue.
panel.amaSeparateNote: AMA is for platform listings under EU 2024/1028 — separate from per-stay AADE declarations.

ama.title: AMA — AADE Property Registration Number
ama.description: Mandatory on listings under EU 2024/1028. Register via myAADE Short-Term Stay Property Registry — separate from per-stay AADE declarations. Licensed tourist accommodations may use ESL / Unique Notification Number instead.
ama.displayedOnListings: Registration number displayed on all platform listings
ama.disclaimer: Not legal advice. AMA ≠ AADE stay declaration. Missing AMA on listings is commonly cited at €5,000.

panel.title: eVisitor guest reporting
panel.description: {city} — Croatia requires every guest registered in eVisitor within 24 hours of arrival and deregistered within 24 hours of departure. Sojourn tax is calculated from eVisitor. Glint prepares guest data; you submit on the official portal.
panel.honestyNote: Glint does not submit to eVisitor automatically. We collect → validate → export CSV/printable kit → you submit on https://www.evisitor.hr/. Phase 2 may integrate the Rhetos API — no live API in this release. You remain legally responsible.
panel.step1: Obtain tourist accommodation categorisation from the Ministry of Tourism
panel.step2: Register your accommodation object on eVisitor and save the object ID
panel.step3: Enable check-in link and collect eVisitor fields for all guests
panel.step4: Prepare export kit (printable + CSV) for check-in and check-out phases
panel.step5: Enter data on eVisitor within 24 hours and mark status in Glint
panel.categorisationSeparateNote: Categorisation is for listing approval under EU 2024/1028 — separate from per-guest eVisitor reporting (mandatory since 2016).
